steps.why: Each package in a default session of its own: its command is absent, it installs alone and is used, and its manual page is text, with no macros. cc installs after it where the use compiles.

steps.script: mkdir /tmp/amy-ninja && cd /tmp/amy-ninja && printf '%s\n' 'rule write' '  command = echo built > $out' 'build out: write' > build.ninja && ninja && test "$(cat out)" = built && man ninja > /dev/null
mkdir /tmp/amy-make && cd /tmp/amy-make && printf 'out:\n\techo made > out\n' > Makefile && make && test "$(cat out)" = made

steps.why: The two ways its manual page gives: a function for a C program, and a program with the standard library.
A page of macros becomes text, and text-page puts it where man reads it.

steps.script: printf '%s\n' '.Dd October 13, 2026' '.Dt PROBE 1' '.Os' '.Sh NAME' '.Nm probe' '.Nd a page of macros' > /tmp/amy.1 && mandoc -T ascii /tmp/amy.1 | grep -q 'a page of macros' && text-page /tmp/amy.1 && grep -qx 'NAME' /usr/share/man/cat1/amy.1
